core_obligations: Reduce to constructing a sheaf of topological rings on the site of affine formal algebraic spaces etale over the space, using the identification of that site with the small etale topos (proof lines 7669-7674).

Introduce the category of representable etale morphisms from an affine formal algebraic space to the space, and use the equivalence given by reduction to obtain the structure sheaf as a presheaf of topological rings (proof lines 7672-7680).

Analyse a covering: a covering is a finite family whose reductions form an etale covering, each member is representable hence affine, and each member is etale by permanence of etaleness (proof lines 7682-7693).

Write the base as a filtered colimit of its defining affine schemes and, for each index, set up the fibre products of the members with that affine scheme; obtain for each index an exact sequence from the sheaf condition for the structure sheaf in the etale topology, noting that the fibre products of the members are the fibre products of the corresponding pieces (proof lines 7694-7721).
Take the filtered limit of the exact sequences, which is exact because limits commute with limits, to obtain the sheaf condition for the structure sheaf of the formal space (proof lines 7721-7727).

Check that the topology on the sections is the one induced from the product: the kernels of the comparison maps form fundamental systems of open submodules on both sides, and each kernel on one side is the inverse image of the corresponding kernel on the other (proof lines 7728-7748).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the site of affine formal etale objects (proof lines 7669-7674).
The structure sheaf as a presheaf via the reduction equivalence (proof lines 7672-7680).
The shape of a covering: finite, representable, affine, etale (proof lines 7682-7693).
Exact sequences at each stage of the filtered system (proof lines 7694-7721).
Filtered limits of exact sequences give the sheaf condition (proof lines 7721-7727).
The limit topology is induced from the product (proof lines 7728-7748).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that every formal algebraic space has a structure sheaf (statement lines 7664-7667). The proof has four distinct parts. First it reduces the problem to constructing the structure sheaf as a sheaf of topological rings on the small etale site of the space, using the identification of that topos with the site of affine formal algebraic spaces etale over it (proof lines 7669-7674). Second it sets up the category of affine formal algebraic spaces etale and representable over the space, observes that reduction is an equivalence from that category to the small etale site, so that the structure sheaf exists as a presheaf and only the sheaf condition remains (proof lines 7672-7680). Third it analyses a covering: a covering corresponds to a finite family whose reductions form an etale covering, and each member is representable hence affine, and etale by permanence, so that after writing the base as a filtered colimit of its defining affine schemes one obtains an exact sequence for each index, and taking the filtered colimit of these exact sequences -- which is legitimate because limits commute with limits -- produces an exact sequence computing the sections of the structure sheaf (proof lines 7682-7727). Fourth, and separately, it must be checked that the topology on the sections is the one induced from the product, which is done by comparing the fundamental systems of open submodules on the two sides (proof lines 7728-7748). The claim is H3: the category-theoretic reduction, the finiteness and affineness analysis of a covering, the limit of exact sequences, and the compatibility of the limit topology are independent pieces of work, and the last of them is a genuine subtlety about topological rings rather than a formality.
